title: MemSentry: A Framework for Detecting Persistent Memory Poisoning in Agentic AI

object.carrier: agent long-term/persistent memory entries (proposed persistent-memory writes derived from emails, webhooks, user-uploaded files, webpages, shared documents); MemSentry intercepts each write before it is committed to active memory

safety_property.statement: Committing a proposed persistent-memory write must not degrade the agentic system's security posture (e.g., suppress security alerts, facilitate privilege escalation, alter trust relationships, override security policies); external-unverified writes are unconditionally quarantined and non-negotiable authority/security policy rules hold regardless of the learned poisoning-risk score. The property structurally weakens for verified insiders with maximal trust (T=1): their dangerous writes are escalated to human Review rather than automatically quarantined.
safety_property.operationalized_as: A deterministic Accept/Review/Quarantine decision per proposed write, computed from source trust T, pluggable semantic risk, attack radius over a 20-asset dependency DAG, access risk, and a signed security-state delta; judged by per-class decision accuracy over 1,000 GPT-4-generated scenarios (100% external quarantine-class detection with all four semantic methods; best classifier 91.7% overall accuracy), an insider authorization sweep, and a held-out contrast set.

capabilities: External adversary: unauthenticated actor injecting content through external channels (emails, webhooks, third-party APIs); can craft arbitrary message content; cannot authenticate as an internal user
Compromised insider (secondary attacker class): authenticated internal user passing identity verification with authorized access to some components, submitting adversarial content that exploits trust
Attacks act through stored memory content only, without modifying model weights or system prompts
assumptions: Source trust T can be computed from origin (external vs. internal), identity verification status, and channel integrity
The protected system can be modeled as a static component-dependency DAG with criticality scores plus an access-control matrix
A pluggable classifier can map an operation to a semantic category and risk score
MemSentry implementation was frozen prior to GPT-4 dataset generation to reduce the risk of overfitting to the evaluation scenarios
not_covered: Coordinated multi-step campaigns (evaluation considers individual memory operations only)
Retrieval-time or post-commit defense (MemSentry is pre-commit; poisoned entries already in persistent memory are out of scope)
Automatic quarantine of verified insiders (T=1 zeroes projected degradation, so insider operations are routed to Review instead)
Dynamic changes in security posture or dependency structure during evaluation (treated as static)

intervention.name: MemSentry
intervention.description: A formal, configuration-driven 9-step pre-admission pipeline that intercepts proposed persistent-memory writes: (1) source trust from provenance/identity/channel; (2) pluggable semantic classification (Regex, TF-IDF+SVM, SBERT+LR, or SetFit) into risk-scored categories; (3) attack radius over a component-dependency DAG; (4) access risk against an access-control matrix; (5-7) current and projected security posture with a signed security-state delta scaled by a persistence factor; (8) a weighted risk score; (9) deterministic rule-based Accept/Review/Quarantine decisions, including a mandatory policy-constraint rule that quarantines any external-unverified source regardless of content. Decisions emit template-based (non-LLM) audit explanations; a counterfactual impact evaluation compares executions with and without the candidate memory to quantify observed blast radius.

results.claim: Across all four semantic methods, MemSentry detected 100% of external quarantine-class attacks in the GPT-4-generated scenario evaluation.
results.comparison: 100% for all four semantic methods (Regex, TF-IDF+SVM, SBERT+LR, SetFit)
results.setting: 1,000 GPT-4-generated scenarios, 70/30 stratified split (300 test samples), 20-asset dependency DAG, 10x20 access-control matrix, external unverified adversary
results.quote: Across all four semantic methods, MemSentry detected 100% of external quarantine-class attacks, while SBERT+LR achieved the best overall performance with 91.7% accuracy and a macro-F1 of 0.908.

results.claim: SBERT+LR is the best overall semantic classifier for the pipeline with 91.7% accuracy and 0.908 macro-F1 on the held-out test split.
results.comparison: best among the four compared semantic methods
results.setting: 300 test samples (70/30 stratified split of 1,000 GPT-4-generated scenarios), SBERT+LR (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 frozen encoder + Logistic Regression)
results.quote: SBERT+LR achieves the best overall performance with 91.7% accuracy and a 0.908 macro-F1 score, while all four methods detect 100% of external quarantine-class threats.

results.claim: The ambiguous Review class is the main differentiator: SBERT+LR reaches 72.2% review accuracy while SetFit drops to 22.2%, despite both having perfect accept and quarantine behavior.
results.setting: 300 test samples, 70/30 split, security-sensitive Review-class operations
results.quote: SBERT+LR is best overall (91.7% accuracy, 0.908 macro-F1), with 72.2% review accuracy. SetFit underperforms on review (22.2%) despite perfect accept and quarantine.

results.claim: TF-IDF+SVM is a strong, computationally inexpensive alternative at 88.0% overall accuracy, while Regex serves as a simple conservative baseline at 78.3%.
results.setting: 300 test samples, 70/30 stratified split of the GPT-4 scenario corpus
results.quote: TF-IDF+SVM offers a strong and computationally inexpensive alternative at 88.0% accuracy, while SetFit performs poorly on the review class at 22.2%. Regex serves as a simple but conservative baseline with 78.3% overall accuracy.

denominator.how_counted: TABLE III: Overall and Macro Metrics (300 Test Samples)

results.claim: For a fully-trusted verified insider (T=1.0), quarantine accuracy is 0% across the entire authorization sweep, a deliberate fail-to-review behavior rather than a detection miss.
results.setting: single insider attacker (internal, verified, T=1.0), authorization swept 0% to 100% in 10% increments, all 1,000 scenarios run through the full pipeline per method
results.quote: The 0% quarantine accuracy in the sweep is therefore a deliberate fail-to-review behavior for trusted insiders, not a detection miss.

denominator.how_counted: authorization sweep: 'All 1000 scenarios are run through the full pipeline for each method'

results.claim: Under full insider authorization, SBERT+LR best preserves review accuracy at 0.91 while SetFit degrades to 0.027.
results.comparison: SBERT+LR 0.91 vs SetFit 0.027 at 100% insider authorization
results.setting: single insider (T=1.0) at 100% authorization, all 1,000 scenarios per method
results.quote: SBERT+LR best preserves review accuracy under high authorization (0.91 at 100%); SetFit degrades most (0.027).

results.claim: On the held-out semantic contrast set, no method reliably distinguishes surface-similar operations with opposing security implications: TF-IDF+SVM resolves only 3/10 pairs, Regex 1/10, and SBERT+LR and SetFit 0/10.
results.setting: 20 held-out contrast items (10 pairs), never used during model fitting, contrasting e.g. authenticated vs. authorized, temporary vs. indefinite
results.quote: None of the evaluated methods reliably resolves the contrast scenarios, with TF-IDF+SVM correctly distinguishing 3/10 pairs, Regex 1/10, and SBERT+LR and SetFit 0/10.

limitations.statement: The evaluation considers individual memory operations only, not coordinated multi-step campaigns.
limitations.quote: The current evaluation considers individual memory operations rather than coordinated multi-step campaigns.

limitations.statement: Insider operations are escalated to Review rather than quarantined unless additional content-based hard rules are introduced.
limitations.quote: Insider operations are escalated to review rather than quarantined unless additional content-based hard rules are introduced.

limitations.statement: Security posture and dependency structure are treated as static during evaluation.
limitations.quote: The security posture and dependency structure are treated as static during evaluation

limitations.statement: Observed contrast-case failures highlight the remaining limitations of lightweight semantic classification.
